tasks.instruction: Read the text below. Choose the correct answer A, B or C for each question.
tasks.text:
THE VOLUNTEER

I started at the animal shelter because of a school requirement. Every student in our year had to complete twenty hours of community work before the end of May, and by April I had done none of them. The shelter was the only place that answered my email.

I had imagined the work would involve playing with puppies. In practice my first three shifts consisted almost entirely of cleaning. There is a great deal of cleaning in an animal shelter, and none of it appears in the photographs on their website. Ewa, who has run the place for eleven years, watched me scrubbing a floor on the second day and remarked, without looking up, that most people leave after the second day.

I stayed, partly out of stubbornness. By the fourth week I had been trusted with the evening feed, which means remembering which of forty animals is on which diet, and which of them will pretend to be starving whatever you give them. I got it wrong twice. Ewa corrected me both times without the slightest suggestion that I was an idiot, which I now understand is a skill.

The part nobody warns you about is the leaving. A dog called Borys had been at the shelter for over a year, long enough that the staff had stopped expecting anything. In my second month a family came for him. I was pleased in a way that surprised me, and also, quite unreasonably, annoyed. Ewa said that feeling never entirely goes away, and that it is the reason the work is worth doing rather than a reason to stop.

My twenty hours finished in the middle of May. I have done another sixty since, and I no longer count them. What I would say to anyone thinking about it is this: do not go for the puppies. Go because you will be more useful than you expect, and because somebody will assume you are competent slightly before you actually are, which turns out to be how people become competent.

items.stem: Why did the writer first go to the shelter?
options: A) A friend had recommended it.
B) It was the only place that replied.
C) The writer had always wanted to work with animals.

items.stem: What was the writer's first impression of the work?
options: A) It was mostly cleaning rather than playing with animals.
B) It was better organised than expected.
C) It was too difficult for a beginner.

items.stem: What does Ewa's remark on the second day suggest?
options: A) She wanted the writer to leave.
B) She did not expect the writer to stay.
C) She thought the floor had been badly cleaned.

items.stem: How did the writer feel when Borys was adopted?
options: C) Pleased and, unexpectedly, resentful at the same time.

items.stem: What does the writer say about the twenty required hours?
options: A) They were completed later than the deadline.

items.stem: What is the writer's main advice to future volunteers?
options: A) Expect to be given responsibility and to grow into it.
B) Choose a shelter with fewer animals.
C) Be prepared to work only with dogs.
